speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I need to evaluate your skin lesions for potential oncologic implications; have you noticed any new moles or spots that are changing in size, shape, or color?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The non-healing, red, crusty lesions on your penis and finger, combined with your heavy smoking history, are concerning; have these lesions been present for more than three weeks or are they bleeding frequently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma. The presence of non-healing, crusty, painless lesions on high-risk sun-exposed skin (finger) and the penile shaft, combined with a significant smoking history and failure of prior treatments for syphilis/eczema, strongly suggests malignancy. I am requesting a biopsy of both lesions to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Biopsy_penile_lesion AND Biopsy_finger_lesion.
